findings_qualitative.value: Jets (high-velocity) are surrounded by intermediate and low-velocity flows; knots indicate episodic ejection

evidence.quote: The high- and intermediate-velocity flows have well-collimated structures surrounded by the low-velocity flow.

claims.hypothesis: The outflow has nested velocity components with distinct launching radii
claims.experiment: PV diagrams and channel maps of CO J=3-2
claims.result: Low, intermediate, high-velocity and entrained components identified
claims.finding: Nested outflow consistent with disk wind

evidence.quote: four distinct components of low ($\lesssim 10\,\text{km\,s}^{-1}$), intermediate ($\sim10-25\,\text{km\,s}^{-1}$) and high ($\gtrsim40\,\text{km\,s}^{-1}$) velocities

claims.hypothesis: Low- and intermediate-velocity flows rotate like the disk
claims.experiment: Perpendicular PV diagrams compared with 13CO/C17O disk/envelope rotation
claims.finding: Gradients are due to outflow rotation

evidence.quote: Thus, we concluded that the velocity gradients in the low- and intermediate-velocity flows are due to the outflow rotation.

claims.hypothesis: Knot periodicity arises from binary orbit or disk instability
claims.experiment: Compare knot intervals with estimated binary orbital period

evidence.quote: Thus, we can safely reject the binary orbital motion scenario as the origin of the periodicity.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Binary orbital motion as origin of knot periodicity rejected

evidence.quote: The time interval ($\Delta t_{\rm dyn} \sim 42 - 48\,\text{yr}$) is too short to explain the periodicity due to the binary orbital motion.

limitations_admitted.value: Protostellar mass not directly determined; launching radii depend on it

evidence.quote: Thus, we need to determine the protostellar mass in the future in order to more accurately estimate the launching radii.

limitations_admitted.value: Optically thin assumption gives lower limits

evidence.quote: Thus, the quantities listed in Table [\[tab:outflowquantities\]](#tab:outflowquantities) may give a lower limit.

referee_caveats_inferred: Launching radius formula depends on assumed M*=0.25 Msun and untested axisymmetry
Rotation only derived for one lobe; blue lobe lacks clear signature
Single fixed Tex=40 K and typical velocities
Jet launching radius assumes terminal velocity equals Keplerian, strongly model dependent
